messages.author: 7e54aa65e5af5819
messages.subject: Re: Cum % Stacked Bar
parts:
Try the following

df$glaucoma <- factor(df$glaucoma)

# This is the quick way of getting a bar chart, but it is not possible
to plot text labels this way
ggplot(data.frame(table(df)), aes(age, Freq, label = Freq, fill =
glaucoma)) +
geom_bar(position = "fill") +
scale_y_continuous(formatter = "percent") +
scale_fill_hue(labels = c("No Glaucoma", "Glaucoma"))

# To plot text labels as well, you would need to calculate the
percentages, and text label positions # manually
x <- ddply(df, .(age, glaucoma), summarise, fr = length
(glaucoma), .drop = F)
x <- ddply(x, .(age), transform, fr_pc = fr/sum(fr))
x <- ddply(x, .(age), transform, txt_pos = cumsum(fr_pc) - fr_pc/2)

ggplot(x, aes(age, fr_pc, label = fr, fill = rev(glaucoma))) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
geom_text(aes(y = txt_pos)) +
scale_y_continuous("", formatter = "percent") +
scale_fill_hue("",labels = c("Glaucoma", "No Glaucoma"))

--
http://learnr.wordpress.com
